title_en: Trinity College Dublin opens a Centre for Land, Food and Medicine
title_zh: 都柏林圣三一学院成立土地、食物与医学中心
practitioners: Centre for Land, Food and Medicine, Trinity College Dublin

body.signal: A Centre for Land, Food and Medicine has started at Trinity College Dublin to address root causes of illness through land and food. Its motto is "When we heal the land we heal the people". Dr Rupa Marya, founder of Deep Medicine Circle in California, moved to Dublin to start it, and Colin P Doherty, Head of the School of Medicine at Trinity, is a co-founder.
body.why_it_works: The centre sits inside a medical school, so work on land and food can connect to clinical teaching and research. Participants include chefs, farmers, doctors, nurses, therapists, food policy workers, historians, artists and climate scientists.
body.transferability: Universities with both a medical faculty and access to farmland could test joint courses. Dr Marya is reported to be open to joint courses or projects with Design Harvests. Outcomes are not yet reported.
body.next_step: Identify one clinician and one farmer near your campus who could co-teach a session on food and health.
body.related_notes: Single source. The editor has not yet opened the source link.

title_en: Aral School fellows share first projects for a post-irrigation economy
title_zh: 咸海学校首批学员发布后灌溉经济项目

body.signal: The Aral School in Nukus shared the first results of its 22-fellow cohort with local publics in Karakalpakstan. Projects include edible fruit canopies for public streets, a vermicompost system for soil health, unglazed clay pot irrigation, local melon varieties grafted onto wild camelthorn roots, cotton husk waste used for mushroom farming, plant-based sun-dried bricks, and a public drinking fountain as an alternative to bottled water.
body.why_it_works: The school is supported by the national government and does not rely on private sector partners. Projects draw on local materials and knowledge, such as traditional water tools and local melon varieties.
body.transferability: John Thackara reads the results as descriptions of future project work, which later cohorts will build on, not finished solutions. Other drylands and post-irrigation regions could adapt the cohort model. Results go on show in Tashkent in September 2026 and in Milan in April 2027.
body.next_step: List the local materials and crop varieties in your region that no design studio has yet worked with.

title_en: Yunhe Forest School marks eleven years of place-based ecological learning
title_zh: 云和森林学校十一年坚持在地生态教育

body.signal: Yunhe Forest School in Zhonglu village, Ganzi Tibetan Autonomous Prefecture, has run project-based ecological learning for eleven years. Its head, Suchin Shu, describes a curriculum that combines Buddhism and ecological restoration, with the mountains and local people as the main teachers. The school cites President Xi Jinping's Two Mountains Theory as its social and ecological framework.
body.why_it_works: In Suchin Shu's account, eleven years of local relationships are the key success factor. She estimates that ten percent of China's parents seek nature connection for their children, which is her own figure.
body.transferability: The school sits in a former mining area, so the model may suit other ex-mining areas, including those along Belt and Road geographies. The school has asked for volunteers to help communicate its work internationally.
body.next_step: Ask which former mining sites in your region have land and local partners for an ecological learning centre.

title_en: UNMEASURED project builds qualitative indicators for agroecology
title_zh: UNMEASURED 项目为生态农业构建定性指标

body.signal: A new project called UNMEASURED, led by Nina Isabella Moeller and supported by the Agroecology Partnership, will develop qualitative indicators for dimensions of agroecology that resist standardisation. These include social cohesion, such as trust networks and mutual aid, cultural resilience, care relations and knowledge sovereignty.
body.why_it_works: Funders and policy makers act on indicators. Qualitative indicators make visible the benefits that yield and carbon figures leave out.
body.transferability: The method could inform how stories on this site report social results. Methods and pilot results are not yet published.
body.next_step: List the social outcomes your project produces that no current metric captures.

title_en: Award-winning Fifth Ecology project treats post-industrial land as fertile ground
title_zh: 获奖项目“第五生态”将后工业用地视为再生沃土

body.signal: Baoyi Huang's project, an award winner in Milan with John Thackara and Lou Yongqi on the jury, frames the Parkwood Springs site through a "Fifth Ecology". In this frame, post-industrial land is fertile ground for renewal. The project proposes the site as a living laboratory of industrial renewal.
body.why_it_works: Former industrial land is often close to cities and available. Treating it as a learning site creates value before full restoration is complete.
body.transferability: Relevant to ex-mining and ex-industrial areas in China and elsewhere. An award concept does not yet show delivery, so the entry is rated Early.
body.next_step: Map the post-industrial sites within an hour of your institution and note who owns them.

title_en: Study finds urban agriculture could meet 28 percent of European vegetable demand
title_zh: 研究显示城市农业可满足欧洲 28% 的蔬菜需求
practitioners: Leibniz Institute of Ecological Urban and Regional Development (IOER)

body.signal: Researchers modelled the potential of urban agriculture in 840 cities across 30 European countries. They report that urban agriculture could produce up to 20 million tonnes of vegetables a year, about 28 percent of Europe's vegetable demand and roughly one third of current regional production.
body.why_it_works: Cities hold roofs, yards and vacant plots close to consumers. A continental estimate gives planners a reason to protect growing space.
body.transferability: John Thackara suggests the figures for Chinese cities could be similar, which has not been tested. The figure is a modelled potential, not current output.
body.next_step: Ask your city planning office whether growing space appears in its land-use plan.

title_en: Kabadiwalla Connect links informal waste systems in India
title_zh: Kabadiwalla Connect 连接印度非正规废弃物回收体系

body.signal: Kabadiwalla Connect works with grassroots and informal waste systems in India. The Design Harvests 3.0 Ten Ideas note proposes a joint pop-up on which informal waste systems work, how they were designed, and how design can connect the actors involved.
body.why_it_works: Informal collectors already move large volumes of material. Connecting them to formal systems builds on what works instead of replacing it.
body.transferability: Chinese cities with informal recyclers could test similar links. The editor should add figures from the organisation's own pages after opening them.
body.next_step: Find out who collects recyclable material informally in your neighbourhood.

title_en: Indian report documents edible wetland plants disappearing from diets
title_zh: 印度报告记录湿地可食用植物正从饮食中消失

body.signal: A 170-page report from India's Centre for Science and Environment documents the loss of wetland area and the decline of traditional edible water plants in diets.
body.why_it_works: Wetland foods link three agendas that usually run apart: food systems, watershed recovery and rural income.
body.transferability: China leads in wetland restoration, but John Thackara notes that the social-ecological dimension is often missing. Wetland projects in Shanghai could add food resilience as a design focus.
body.next_step: Ask a wetland restoration team near you which edible plants grew on the site before.

title_en: Scottish catchment publishes gap analysis for landscape finance and governance
title_zh: 苏格兰流域发布景观融资与治理差距分析

body.signal: Bioregioning Tayside published a stocktake and gap analysis of landscape-scale finance and governance innovation in Scotland, focused on the Ericht catchment.
body.why_it_works: A gap analysis gives funders and agencies a shared list of what is missing before they commit money.
body.transferability: Catchment authorities elsewhere could use the same stocktake format. The analysis is a plan, not a delivered programme.
body.next_step: Draft a one-page list of what your watershed or district lacks in finance and governance.

title_en: Dutch Landscape Leadership Lab shifts government toward facilitating bottom-up change
title_zh: 荷兰景观领导力实验室推动政府转向支持自下而上的变革

body.signal: Oogst van Morgen, a two-year Landscape Leadership Lab in the Netherlands, tests how governments and regional stakeholders can shift from controlling processes to facilitating bottom-up transformation. It is part of a European movement experimenting with landscape-based collaboration.
body.why_it_works: A fixed two-year format gives public officials time to practise a new role alongside farmers and residents.
body.transferability: The lab format could suit Chinese townships working on rural revitalisation. Results of the first cycle are not yet reported.
body.next_step: Name the one decision in your project that local stakeholders could take instead of the lead institution.

title_en: French course trains city dwellers to set up rural eco-places
title_zh: 法国课程培训城市居民创建乡村生态社区

body.signal: Frédéric Bosqué launched Rurality 2.0, a 12-week training course on how to finance an eco-place in transition and leave the city. John Thackara reports that 57 percent of city dwellers in France say they dream of leaving the city to live closer to nature.
body.why_it_works: Many people have already moved on their own. A structured course helps them plan finance and community before they go.
body.transferability: Comparable demand may exist among Chinese urban residents interested in rural revitalisation. The 57 percent figure is a survey of wishes, not of moves.
body.next_step: Ask your rural partners what newcomers most often get wrong in their first year.

title_en: Kentucky Urban-Rural Exchange marks ten years across 65 counties
title_zh: 肯塔基城乡交流项目十年覆盖 65 个县

body.signal: The Kentucky Urban-Rural Exchange (RUX) is ten years old. Kentuckians from 65 counties have exchanged stories, meals, traditions and ideas, and an annual gathering brings together teachers, farmers, artists, attorneys, students, factory workers, nurses and community leaders.
body.why_it_works: It works in Appalachia, an economically marginal region, through many small grassroots activities that John Thackara describes as "a pebble in a pond making ripples of change".
body.transferability: Its focus on urban-rural exchange sets it apart from traditional regional development programmes, which makes it a reference for Design Harvests in China.
body.next_step: Plan one shared meal that brings urban and rural participants of your project together.

title_en: Cambridge team wins 4.6 million pounds to map Anglesey's eco-social assets
title_zh: 剑桥团队获 460 万英镑绘制安格尔西岛生态社会资产地图
practitioners: University of Cambridge, Department of Architecture

body.signal: A Cambridge-led team secured 4.6 million pounds through the Green Transition Ecosystems call, run by the Arts and Humanities Research Council with the Design Museum's Future Observatory, to build a community open map platform of eco-social assets for the Isle of Anglesey.
body.why_it_works: Public research money funds a platform that residents can use, which links design research to local decisions.
body.transferability: John Thackara notes a risk that a map is not the destination, and that a gap remains between policy maps and changemakers on the ground. Rural regions in China could adapt the mapping approach with a delivery plan attached.
body.next_step: List the eco-social assets in your district that appear on no official map.

title_en: France invests 130 million euros in urban-rural tiers-lieux
title_zh: 法国投入 1.3 亿欧元建设城乡“第三空间”

body.signal: The French government announced an investment of 130 million euros in tiers-lieux, hybrid spaces that combine coworking, micro-fabrication, connected campuses, shared workshops, fablabs and makerspaces. Most are being established in old factories and other disused sites.
body.why_it_works: An interministerial recovery programme funds the network, so local groups can open spaces without carrying the full capital cost.
body.transferability: One group, Lustrac, estimates that 35 million French citizens want to leave big cities and that 20,000 small communes could welcome them, as its own figure. Chinese townships with disused industrial buildings could test similar hubs.
body.next_step: List the disused buildings in your town that could host shared workshops.

title_en: Researcher publishes roadmap for microbiome-inspired green infrastructure
title_zh: 研究者发布受微生物组启发的绿色基础设施路线图

body.signal: Jake Robinson published a roadmap for Microbiome Inspired Green Infrastructure (MIGI), which designs urban green space to support beneficial environmental microbes and human health.
body.why_it_works: The approach links planting and surface design to measurable exposure to microbial diversity.
body.transferability: John Thackara proposes a campus as a test site, generating data on links between microbial diversity exposure and health, and on the effect of design interventions. Health outcomes are still at research stage.
body.next_step: Ask your campus estates team whether any planting plan considers soil and microbial diversity.
